title: Hochul and Blakeman Clash Over ICE and Sanctuary Policy in Only NY Debate
excerpt: A Bronx ICE shooting, Nassau County's abandoned ICE agreement and competing claims about crime dominated the sole Hochul-Blakeman debate before November 3.
body:
• Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Bruce Blakeman clashed over ICE, sanctuary policy and a recent Bronx ICE shooting in their only scheduled debate on October 13, three weeks before the November 3 election.
  • Blakeman said Nassau County cooperated with ICE to remove more than 2,000 people with criminal records and pledged to end New York's sanctuary status on day one; Hochul said ICE is out of control and that local police can still cooperate on nearly 200 crimes.
  • Polls cited in coverage put Hochul ahead by roughly 9 to 19 points; early voting runs October 24 to November 1.
  • For immigrant families in New York: the fight is over a state law restricting formal local cooperation agreements with federal immigration authorities — the policy that forced Nassau County to abandon its ICE agreement.

New York's governor's race turned on immigration on Tuesday night. In their only scheduled debate, Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, spent long stretches arguing over Immigration and Customs Enforcement, sanctuary policy and a recent ICE shooting in the Bronx, according to reports by the New York Post, WAMC and Fox News.

The 60-minute debate on NY1 came three weeks before Election Day on November 3.

The shooting that framed the debate

Moderators opened with an ICE operation in which agents shot a man during an attempted arrest while a 5-year-old was in the back seat, in the Marble Hill area. WAMC reported that Blakeman answered by pointing to the state law Hochul supported. Hochul answered by faulting Blakeman for not condemning the shooting itself.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=V9CxtajtR_k

"He'd be fine if ICE agents shoot into cars, not knowing who's inside, and could have killed a 5-year-old child"

— Gov. Kathy Hochul, during the debate, via New York Post

The Post identified the man shot as a Dominican national and alleged gang member who was shot as he tried to flee an arrest in a car, and noted the NYPD said no city officers were involved in the shooting. Blakeman's question, repeated across all three reports, was why the man was in New York at all.

Two records, two claims about safety

Blakeman said cooperation worked in his county. He cited the removal of more than 2,000 migrants with criminal records from Nassau County and said that cooperation happened without raids on schools, hospitals, daycare centres or churches. He blamed Hochul's sanctuary policies for the Bronx case and for other crimes, and pressed her in a separate Fox News-reported exchange to apologise to families of people killed by immigrants in the country illegally, including the family of Sheridan Gorman, an 18-year-old from Yorktown.

https://x.com/seanhannity/status/2110353679215726840

Hochul did not give the apology Blakeman asked for. Fox News reported she called all crimes heartbreaking, pointed to billions spent to support law enforcement and to crime driven down to historic lows, and countered by raising Americans shot by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis in January. In the Post and WAMC accounts she also stressed the limit is not total: local police can still work with federal authorities on nearly 200 crimes, and she accused Nassau officers of being distracted by acting as ICE agents.

The policy underneath the argument

The mechanism is a state law, included in this year's budget, that restricts formal cooperation agreements between local governments and the federal government on immigration. WAMC reported the law forced Blakeman to abandon Nassau County's agreement with ICE. Blakeman has promised to remove the state's sanctuary status on day one if elected. Hochul defended the limits as keeping local police focused on local crime rather than deputised as immigration agents.

That distinction matters for Indian and other immigrant communities in New York, who live under the same state framework whether they are in Nassau County, Queens or upstate. A change of governor would not change federal immigration law, but it would change whether county and state agencies sign and staff cooperation agreements with ICE.

Cost of living, Trump and the state of the race

Immigration did not take the whole hour. Blakeman blamed Hochul for high taxes, spending and utility bills and pledged to cut electric bills in half, including by allowing fracking, banned in New York since 2014. Hochul touted rebate checks of up to $200, a moratorium on large data centres, and repeatedly tied Blakeman to President Donald Trump, bringing him up more than a dozen times, the Post reported. Blakeman replied that she raised Trump to avoid her own record.

WAMC cited polls showing Hochul ahead by 9 to 19 points; the Post put recent polling at a 9-to-11-point gap. Early voting runs October 24 to November 1.
